argument_markdown:
## Source-backed inputs

The packet fixes F = O(4) ⊕ O(5) and W_5 = (O_{P(E^∨)}(2) ⊗ γ^*O(-5))|_C; the negative sign is essential because W_5 is the f_2=5 summand of O(2)⊗γ^*F^∨, not the O(5) summand of F. The degree formula from SRC-0004 Lemma 10.6 is deg(W_f|_C) = 4g+12-4f. It also gives the CE obstruction decomposition into H^0(C,ω_C⊗W_f^∨(Γ)). FND-0062, FND-0063, and FND-0074 admit these as the actual fibrewise CE obstruction summands in the balanced (6,6) case.

FND-0064 and FND-0075 state that Conf_6 → Div^6_red is a finite étale S_6-torsor on stacks, not on coarse moduli in the presence of automorphisms. FND-0087 requires compatible base change/reduction rather than reduction of only the ordered source.

## Proved steps

For g=6, deg W_4 = 20 and deg W_5 = 16. Since deg ω_C = 10 and deg Γ = 6,

deg(ω_C⊗W_4^∨(Γ)) = 10-20+6 = -4,

deg(ω_C⊗W_5^∨(Γ)) = 10-16+6 = 0.

The negative-degree f=4 line bundle has no section. A degree-zero line bundle on a smooth projective curve has a nonzero section exactly when it is trivial. Moreover,

ω_C⊗W_5^∨(Γ) ≅ O_C

is equivalent to

O_C(Γ) ≅ W_5⊗ω_C^{-1} = L.

Thus the f=5 obstruction is nonzero exactly on the stated Abel–Jacobi incidence. Because the f=4 summand is zero and SRC-0004 identifies the direct sum as the CE obstruction, evaluation fails exactly on that incidence. This polarity is essential: the obstruction is nonzero, not zero, when O_C(Γ) ≅ L.

The relative Abel–Jacobi fibre product I_L^red constructs the incidence without identifying it with Proj π_*L. Base-changing the stack torsor Conf_6 → Div^6_red along I_L^red gives the finite étale S_6-torsor Z_AJ^ord → I_L^red. On every geometric fibre, the preceding calculation identifies the points of I_L^red with the reduced-support CE failure divisors.

## Computational hypotheses

None. No finite experiment or rank computation is used.

## Gaps and scope boundaries

FND-0046 leaves open comparison between the determinantal/Fitting scheme structure of the relative CE failure locus and the Abel–Jacobi fibre product; only geometric-point equality is proved here. FND-0047 prevents replacing the incidence by Proj π_*L when h^0(L) jumps without additional base-change work. FND-0083 shows that Riemann–Roch does not prove fibrewise nonemptiness of the reduced-support or ordered incidence. FND-0052, FND-0067, and FND-0091 prevent claims that the balanced model is a closed pure-codimension substack or the full failure locus in M_{6,6}. Dimensions, components, stabilizers, local complete-intersection properties, and unbalanced splitting types remain for later DAG nodes, as emphasized by FND-0058, FND-0060, FND-0068, FND-0069, and FND-0086. No Tate-support or assembly conclusion is claimed.

## Dependencies and failed routes

TASK.json supplies no blocked dependencies, dependency artifacts, input attempts, or confirmation reviews, so none are inferred or cited. The blocked routes vcd-only-vanishing, undecorated-cgp-top-weight-graph-complex, point-count-without-degree-parity-separation, and forgetful-map-renaming-local-system-unknown are not used. Respectively, they do not construct this CE incidence: FND-0035 shows the vcd argument gives no required vanishing; FND-0032 concerns the wrong weight corner; the packet admits no parity-separated point-count input; and FND-0036–FND-0037 leave the mixed-local-system extension unresolved. No blocked route is reopened and new_inputs is empty.

This proves only C66-GEO-Z in its weakest fibrewise and stacky reduced-support form. It does not resolve RED-0001 or any downstream GEO-H0, GEO-COMP, TATE-SUPPORT, or TATE-ASSEMBLY node.

claims.statement: For balanced genus-6 tetragonal covers, W_5 is the f_2=5 summand (O_{P(E^∨)}(2)⊗γ^*O(-5))|_C, deg W_5=16, and L=W_5⊗ω_C^{-1} has degree 6.
For every effective degree-6 divisor Γ on a smooth balanced geometric fibre, H^0(C,ω_C⊗W_4^∨(Γ))=0 because the line bundle has degree -4.
For every effective degree-6 divisor Γ on a smooth balanced geometric fibre, H^0(C,ω_C⊗W_5^∨(Γ)) is nonzero exactly when O_C(Γ)≅W_5⊗ω_C^{-1}.
The geometric points of the reduced-support Abel–Jacobi incidence I_L^red are exactly the balanced reduced-support CE evaluation-failure divisors for the chosen tetragonal cover.
The ordered incidence Z_AJ^ord→I_L^red is a finite étale S_6-torsor on stacks, obtained by base change from Conf_6→Div^6_red.

summary: The balanced degree-six failure condition is identified exactly on smooth geometric fibres with the Abel–Jacobi incidence O_C(Γ) ≅ W_5⊗ω_C^{-1}. Its ordered distinct-point model is the finite étale S_6-pullback over the reduced-support open. The result does not identify a global determinantal failure scheme, the unbalanced locus, components, codimension, or Tate contributions.
theorem_statement: Theorem (balanced geometric-point evaluation-failure incidence at (6,6)). Let B^bal be the stack of smooth genus-6 degree-4 covers with balanced Casnati–Ekedahl splitting F = O_{P^1}(4) ⊕ O_{P^1}(5), with universal curve C/B^bal. Use the CE convention W_5 = (O_{P(E^∨)}(2) ⊗ γ^*O_{P^1}(-5))|_C, the f_2=5 summand of (O(2) ⊗ γ^*F^∨)|_C, and put L = W_5 ⊗ ω_C^{-1}. Let Div^6_red(C/B^bal) be the reduced-support open in the relative degree-6 effective-divisor space, let AJ: Div^6_red(C/B^bal) → Pic^6(C/B^bal) be Abel–Jacobi, and define I_L^red as the fibre product of AJ with the section [L]. Define Z_AJ^ord = Conf_6(C/B^bal) ×_{Div^6_red(C/B^bal)} I_L^red. Then for every smooth geometric fibre C and every effective degree-6 divisor Γ: (1) H^0(C, ω_C ⊗ W_4^∨(Γ)) = 0; (2) H^0(C, ω_C ⊗ W_5^∨(Γ)) is nonzero if and only if O_C(Γ) ≅ L, and hence CE evaluation fails on Γ if and only if O_C(Γ) ≅ L; and (3) Z_AJ^ord → I_L^red is a finite étale S_6-torsor on stacks. Thus the geometric points of I_L^red are exactly the balanced reduced-support CE evaluation-failure divisors for the chosen cover. No equality of relative determinantal/Fitting scheme structures is asserted.
